question: Fuel burned per hour rises with the cube of speed. Slow a ship from 20 to 16 knots: what happens to fuel per voyage?
answer: Falls to about 64%. Per hour, 0.8 cubed is 0.51, but the slower ship spends 1.25 times as long at sea, so per voyage the saving follows the square: 0.8 squared is 0.64. A line keeping a weekly service must also add ships to the loop, which eats part of the gain.
move: When a rate falls, check whether the time it runs for grows.
trap: Applying the cube to the whole voyage and forgetting the extra hours.
source: Notteboom & Vernimmen, Journal of Transport Geography, 2009
reference: Notteboom & Vernimmen, The effect of high fuel costs on liner service configuration in container shipping, Journal of Transport Geography, 2009
